To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clustering of DRGs at z ~ 2 is consistent with standard halo occupation models if the satellite DRG fraction is 44%.
the formation of distant red galaxies correlates with large-scale structure at fixed halo mass and that satellite galaxies are more likely to be distant red galaxies than central galaxies.

the clustering of DRGs is well fit by a halo occupation model, that satellite DRG formation is more efficient than central DRG formation, that satellite DRGs must know they will become satellites well before they are accreted, and that satellite DRGs have a shorter quenching timescales than central DRGs.

the evolution of the galaxy population, and in particular the evolution of the red sequence.
the formation of red and dead galaxies at high redshifts and how it is affected by environment.
the clustering of distant galaxies and the formation of red galaxies in the distant universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of satellite DRGs is more strongly tied to the environment at fixed halo masses than central DRGs.

the clustering of z = 2 DRGs can be fit by standard halo occupation models if one assumes that the formation of satellites is more efficient than that of centrals, that satellite DRGs are quenched within ~500 Myr of their accretions into the halo, that ~30% are non-star forming at z = 0, and that the quenching of centrals is more efficient at higher halo mass.
DRGs are a mixed population of galaxies, and that the clustering and halo occupation distribution of this population are consistent with expectations from standard halo occupation models.

, at fixed stellar mass, satellite galaxies are more efficient at becoming DRGs than central galaxies, and that the formation of satellite DRGs is strongly correlated with large-scale environment.

the clustering of DRGs is consistent with standard models, but that DRGs are a more extreme class of galaxies than previously thought, and that the DRG selection may be a useful probe of halo assembly and evolution.
